skim: The Philippine ferry MV June Aster’s death toll climbed to 76 with 13 still unaccounted for, as new reporting exposed a documented safety culture of “lip service” at operator 21 Air, whose crew had logged as little as five months on the Boeing 767 before the fatal runway overrun.

Houthi forces seized Yemen’s Mayun (Perim) Island, completing their hold over both channels of the Bab el-Mandeb strait, as Saudi Arabia kept its East-West pipeline shut after a drone strike traced to Iraq and Trump predicted the Iran war would end “right after the mid-terms.”

Anthropic disclosed that Iranian, Chinese and Russian state-linked actors and a Yemeni Houthi cell tried to weaponize Claude — for naval targeting, missile-guidance troubleshooting, Uyghur identification and covert recruitment — while Sam Altman said OpenAI is open to slowing its own development and ruled out a 2026 IPO.
Oracle’s cloud infrastructure revenue more than doubled to $7.4 billion and total sales rose 30% to $19.3 billion, topping the growth guidance it had set ahead of the print.

Xi Jinping made his first visit to India in seven years, with Modi and Xi backing a “fair, reasonable” settlement of their boundary dispute as BRICS adopted a New Delhi Declaration condemning unilateral tariffs and calling for UN Security Council reform.

stories.headline: Philippine Ferry Fire Death Toll More Than Doubles to 76
stories.body: The confirmed death toll from the MV June Aster fire off Palawan’s Coron island jumped to 76, with 13 people still unaccounted for, after rescuers pulled 41 more charred remains from the vessel’s economy accommodation section on Saturday alone, per ABC News (Sep 13). Survivors told investigators “two explosions were heard inside the vessel” shortly before the blaze tore through the 174-foot ferry within seconds; Coast Guard official Geronimo Tuvilla said the priority now is identifying victims and pinning down the cause.

stories.headline: Miami Cargo Crash Puts Amazon’s Boeing 767 Operator Under Scrutiny
stories.body: New reporting on the September 6 Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami International — which killed five ground workers when the Boeing 767 overran the runway at roughly 180mph and struck two vehicles — has turned to carrier 21 Air, whose captain held 767 certification for under five months and whose first officer for under 18 months, per NPR (Sep 12). A departing 21 Air safety director had written that leadership paid “lip service” to safety protocols, and aviation consultant Ross Aimer said “in my 60 years of flying, I’ve never seen such a terrible performance from a crew” — the third major accident involving a 767 flying for Amazon since 2019.

stories.headline: Céline Dion Returns to the Stage After Stiff Person Syndrome Battle
stories.body: Céline Dion opened a sold-out 16-show residency at the Plenitude Arena outside Paris on Saturday, her first shows since revealing in 2022 that she has stiff person syndrome, a rare neurological condition causing rigid limbs and severe muscle spasms, per NPR (Sep 12). Visibly emotional after opening with “On Ne Change Pas,” the Quebec singer told the crowd, “I had promised myself not to cry… I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage. So here I am, singing for you and singing for me, singing live!”

stories.headline: England Completes Historic 3–0 Whitewash of Pakistan
stories.body: England beat Pakistan by eight wickets at Edgbaston on Saturday to complete a 3–0 series sweep, having already won the first two Tests by innings margins of 103 and 194 runs. “We’re not the finished article. We’re not going to kid ourselves,” said England captain Joe Root, while Pakistan’s Babar Azam admitted “we need to sit down and admit our mistakes, and then work out our best XI,” per The National (Sep 12).

stories.headline: Norris Snatches Pole From Antonelli in Thrilling Madring Qualifying
stories.body: Lando Norris beat championship leader Kimi Antonelli to pole for the Spanish Grand Prix by just 0.011 seconds, with Max Verstappen third, in a session Norris called “probably one of the best laps I’ve done in my career,” per Sky Sports (Sep 12). Antonelli still leads the championship by 66 points with nine rounds left, but Norris has won three of the last four races heading into today’s race at the brand-new Madring circuit.

stories.headline: Manchester City and Arsenal Share Early Pace Ahead of Derby
stories.body: Manchester City and Arsenal sit level atop the Premier League on nine points from three straight wins, the only unbeaten sides after Hull City’s promotion-season surge to third, per worldfootball.net (Sep 12) standings. City travel to Old Trafford for the season’s first Manchester derby later today, with Pep Guardiola’s side looking to open daylight before the international break.

stories.headline: Oracle’s Cloud Revenue More Than Doubles
stories.body: Oracle’s fiscal Q1 2027 results showed cloud infrastructure revenue up 121% to $7.4 billion and total revenue up 30% to $19.3 billion, beating estimates and topping the 58-64% cloud growth guidance Oracle had set ahead of the print, per Quartz (Sep 10). The results extend a run of triple-digit cloud infrastructure growth as Oracle continues building out AI-driven data-center capacity for its enterprise customers.

stories.headline: Boeing’s Air Force Contract Ceiling Nearly Quadruples to $19.1 Billion
stories.body: The US Air Force Life Cycle Management Center raised the ceiling on an existing Boeing contract to $19.1 billion from $5.7 billion, with the modification covering Foreign Military Sales to Japan and Israel and provisions for “future country partners,” per Investing.com (Sep 11). The original 2019 contract runs through April 2035 and is administered out of Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio.

stories.headline: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Wants to Say Less, and Markets Are Unsettled
stories.body: Kevin Warsh is breaking with the decades-long practice of Federal Reserve chairs signalling their next policy moves well in advance, opting instead for a more reserved communication style that has left investors uneasy about reading the central bank’s intentions, per NPR (Sep 12). The shift comes as traders price in roughly 90% odds of a rate move at the coming meeting following hotter-than-expected August inflation data.

stories.headline: Anthropic Says Iran, China, Russia and Houthi Cell Tried to Weaponize Claude
stories.body: An eight-month Anthropic threat investigation found Iranian operators used Claude for naval targeting and domestic surveillance of opposition figures, a Yemeni Houthi weapons cell used Claude Code to develop and troubleshoot rocket and missile guidance software after failed test launches, Chinese actors used it to identify Uyghurs in Syria via social media for covert recruitment, and Russian actors explored autonomous drone-targeting work, per Axios (Sep 12). Anthropic said it blocked access when Claude refused dangerous requests from state-backed researchers, though some then turned to rival AI systems with weaker safeguards.

stories.headline: Amodei Urges Rivals to ‘Pace the Frontier’ as Altman Delays OpenAI IPO
stories.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published “We Must Pace the Frontier,” proposing frontier labs grant permanent, employee-level access to third-party safety evaluators and pursue international agreements limiting recursive self-improvement, warning that a misaligned “swarm with greater capabilities… could cause catastrophic damage” within 6-12 months, citing the roughly 1,200-agent OpenAI-Hugging Face incident, per Unite.AI (Sep 12). Separately, OpenAI’s Sam Altman told staff the company is “open to slowing the development of cutting-edge” AI and hopes rivals follow, telling Fortune that “given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment” for a 2026 IPO.

stories.headline: Houthis Seize Mayun Island, Taking Full Control of Bab el-Mandeb
stories.body: Houthi fighters captured Yemen’s Mayun (Perim) Island after government forces withdrew, giving the group command of both channels of the Bab el-Mandeb strait — which carries over 25% of global seaborne crude and roughly a third of world container shipping — per Euronews (Sep 12). A local official said “boats carrying armed Houthi fighters reached Mayun Island after government forces withdrew from it yesterday,” while Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed navigation remains safe “for all companies except Saudi ships, which have already been banned.”

stories.headline: Trump Says Iran War Will End ‘Right After’ the Midterms
stories.body: Speaking in Dublin, Trump said of the Iran war, “I think very soon, I think it’ll be right after the mid-terms, actually,” and predicted “oil will come tumbling down when that happens,” per Newslooks (Sep 12). Asked whether Iran was behind the drone strike that forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West pipeline, Trump said “I think they are. Probably, they are,” while also claiming “the Houthis called us and they don’t want to fight with us.”

stories.headline: Modi and Xi Back ‘Fair, Reasonable’ Border Settlement as BRICS Adopts Declaration
stories.body: On his first visit to India in seven years, Xi Jinping told Modi “China and India are partners, not rivals,” representing “each other’s development opportunities, not threats,” while Modi said “peace and tranquility in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations,” per Spokesman.com (Sep 12). BRICS separately adopted a consensus New Delhi Declaration condemning unilateral tariffs and sanctions and calling for UN Security Council reform, despite divisions between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia war.

fixtures.headline: Manchester Derby Kicks Off Later Today
fixtures.body: Table-toppers Manchester City travel to Old Trafford for the season’s first Manchester derby, aiming to press their advantage before the international break.

fixtures.headline: India Chase Asia Cup Glory Against Sri Lanka in Dubai
fixtures.body: India and Sri Lanka meet in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final in Dubai, a spin-heavy rematch after Sri Lanka’s semi-final win over Pakistan.

fixtures.headline: Spanish Grand Prix Race Day at Madring
fixtures.body: Lando Norris starts from his first Madring pole just 0.011s ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli, with the grid’s tightest qualifying of the season setting up a tense street-circuit race.

portfolio.headline: Oracle Cloud Revenue More Than Doubles
portfolio.body: Oracle’s fiscal Q1 cloud infrastructure revenue jumped 121% to $7.4 billion and total revenue rose 30% to $19.3 billion, beating estimates, per Quartz (Sep 10). See Business & Markets.

portfolio.headline: Boeing’s Air Force Contract Ceiling Raised to $19.1 Billion
portfolio.body: A contract modification lifted the ceiling on an existing Boeing Air Force deal to $19.1 billion from $5.7 billion, covering Foreign Military Sales to Japan and Israel, per Investing.com (Sep 11). See Business & Markets.

portfolio.headline: Rackspace Joins Nvidia’s Cloud Partner Program
portfolio.body: Rackspace joined Nvidia’s Cloud Partner Program and unveiled an “Institutional Sovereign Pod” combining Nvidia Blackwell chips with Palantir Foundry/AIP for regulated enterprises and governments, per Benzinga (Sep 10). CEO Gajen Kandiah said “enterprise AI is becoming production infrastructure… the question is no longer simply who provides the GPU.”

portfolio.headline: Arm Rides Broad Optimism on Agentic AI Chip Push
portfolio.body: Arm Holdings outperformed the broader chip sector on no single announcement, with investors instead pointing to its expansion into agentic AI platforms — including a new Compute Subsystem for Mobile and neural-capable Mali GPU designs — and growing adoption of its Neoverse server platforms among cloud providers, per TradingKey (Sep 11). Street consensus rates the stock Buy with an average price target of $278.58.

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike Slips as Wedbush Trims Post-Split Target
portfolio.body: Wedbush cut its CrowdStrike price target to $250 from $720 to reflect the company’s recent 4-for-1 stock split, while keeping an Outperform rating, even as Nvidia’s Jensen Huang separately highlighted CrowdStrike’s AI-powered security work, per WhyIsStock (Sep 12). No single negative catalyst drove the modest pullback beyond the reprice.

stories.headline: Modi and Putin Set $100 Billion Trade Target, Discuss Su-57 and BrahMos
stories.body: In BRICS-sidelines talks, Modi and Putin set an ambitious $100 billion bilateral trade target by 2030 and discussed BrahMos missile upgrades, a Su-57 fighter jet supply proposal, and completing outstanding S-400 deliveries, per The Week (Sep 11). Putin invited Modi to Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit, which Modi accepted, while both leaders also discussed India’s civil nuclear reactor plans and Modi “reiterated that India was ready to help resolve conflicts” over Ukraine.

stories.headline: India-China Reset Brings Restored Flights, Eased Investment Curbs
stories.body: Beyond the border-settlement language, Xi’s visit produced concrete economic steps: India has loosened restrictions on Chinese company investment and the two countries have restored direct flights between them, per Spokesman.com (Sep 12). Xi separately promoted a World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization at BRICS, urging members toward collaborative, open-source AI development.

stories.headline: Three Arrested as Portsmouth Face-Covering Ban Faces First Test
stories.body: Rival anti-immigration and counter-protests returned to Portsmouth on Saturday under newly enforced face-covering restrictions, resulting in three arrests including a 76-year-old man for wearing a black scarf covering his face and a 16-year-old for suspected violent disorder tied to the previous weekend’s unrest, per Time News (Sep 12). Hampshire and Isle of Wight Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones said the ban “was implemented equally and impartially for everyone involved.”

stories.headline: Qatar Condemns Iranian Attacks on Five Arab States
stories.body: Qatar’s Foreign Ministry condemned Iranian attacks on Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait and the UAE as “a flagrant violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the targeted states, and a blatant breach of international law, the UN Charter, and the principles of good-neighborly relations,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 12). The statement also condemned Houthi targeting of civilian facilities and commercial vessels in the Red Sea.

stories.headline: QNB: AI Could Expose 40% of Emerging-Market Jobs
stories.body: A QNB report said the global AI market could grow twenty-five-fold to about $4.8 trillion by 2033 per UNCTAD estimates, while the IMF puts roughly 40% of emerging-market jobs at risk of AI exposure, citing India’s $300 billion IT outsourcing sector where the Nifty IT index has fallen 15% this year even as broader emerging-market equities gained 20%, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 12). QNB called for “decisive action across three fronts”: digital infrastructure, data ecosystems and skills investment.

doha_events.headline: Qatar Fintech Expo Returns to Doha Festival City
doha_events.body: The Qatar Fintech Expo runs September 29-30 at Doha Festival City, bringing together fintech startups, investors and policymakers with an exhibition hall, panel discussions, startup pitch sessions and a GFI Award Ceremony bridging traditional finance and digital innovation.

doha_events.headline: Asian U14 Tennis Championship Comes to Khalifa Complex
doha_events.body: The Asian U14 Tennis Championship runs September 28 through October 3 at the Khalifa International Tennis and Squash Complex, drawing the region’s top junior players as part of a packed September-into-October sporting calendar in Doha.

doha_events.headline: National Museum Opens Mahara Perfume-Making Workshop
doha_events.body: The National Museum of Qatar’s Mahara Programme runs a perfume-making workshop for women 18 and over from September 14-16, part of the museum’s ongoing craft and heritage programming.

doha_events.headline: Liwan Design Studios Hosts ‘Silver Soups’ Image-Making Workshop
doha_events.body: Liwan Design Studios and Labs runs its “Silver Soups — Alternative Image-Making” workshop on September 15-16, exploring experimental photographic techniques as part of the studio’s September craft programme.
